The ideal candidate should understand audience behavior, lead generation strategies, campaign optimization, and how to select the right advertising platform based on a business’s target audience and objectives. 2. Key Responsibilities Paid Advertising Campaign Management • Plan, create, launch, and manage advertising campaigns across Meta Ads, Google Ads, and LinkedIn Ads. • Set up campaigns, ad sets, ad groups, targeting parameters, placements, bidding strategies, and budgets. • Manage the complete campaign lifecycle, from research and setup to optimization and reporting. • Select suitable advertising platforms and campaign objectives based on each client’s business model and marketing goals. Lead Generation and Audience Targeting • Develop strategies to generate relevant, qualified leads for different industries and business types. • Conduct audience research to identify the right demographics, interests, locations, job titles, industries, and buyer segments. • Build custom audiences, lookalike audiences, remarketing audiences, and relevant B2B & B2C audience segments. • Understand customer intent and the buyer journey to improve lead generation and conversion rates. • Research and identify suitable target markets for both B2B and B2C campaigns. Lead Verification and Quality Management • Monitor and evaluate the quality of leads generated through paid advertising campaigns. • Identify irrelevant, duplicate, invalid, or low-intent leads and recommend corrective actions. • Analyze lead quality and conversion feedback to refine targeting and campaign strategies. • Coordinate with sales and client teams to understand lead outcomes and improve lead-to-customer conversion rates. • Maintain accurate lead tracking and performance records. A/B Testing and Campaign Optimization • Conduct A/B tests on ad creatives, headlines, copy, audience segments, landing pages, and campaign settings. • Analyze campaign performance and identify opportunities to improve results. • Optimize budgets, bids, targeting, placements, and conversion paths. • Reduce cost per lead (CPL) while maintaining lead quality. • Scale successful campaigns based on performance data and business objectives. Tracking, Analytics, and Reporting • Set up and monitor conversion tracking, pixels, and campaign measurement systems. • Use Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Google Analytics 4 (GA4), and Google Tag Manager. • Track and analyze key performance indicators, including: – Cost Per Lead (CPL) – Cost Per Click (CPC) – Click-Through Rate (CTR) – Conversion Rate (CVR) – Cost Per Acquisition (CPA) – Return on Ad Spend (ROAS), where applicable • Prepare weekly and monthly campaign performance reports. • Provide actionable recommendations based on campaign data and lead quality. Landing Pages and Conversion Optimization • Evaluate landing pages, lead forms, and conversion journeys to identify performance gaps. • Recommend improvements to landing page content, forms, calls to action, and user experience. • Work with the website, content, and creative teams to improve conversion rates. Team Collaboration and Client Support • Collaborate with content writers, designers, video editors, sales teams, and account managers. • Share campaign requirements and provide feedback on ad creatives and messaging. • Understand client objectives and translate them into effective advertising strategies. • Maintain campaign documentation, budgets, and performance records. 3. Preferred Qualifications • Experience managing campaigns for B2B and B2C businesses. • Experience in industries such as SaaS, IT services, education, real estate, and D2C. • Knowledge of CRM platforms, marketing automation, and lead management systems. • Familiarity with Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics 4, Meta Pixel, and LinkedIn Insight Tag. • Experience with conversion rate optimization and landing page performance analysis. • Relevant certifications from Google, Meta, or LinkedIn are an advantage. 5. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) The candidate’s performance will be evaluated based on: • Quality and relevance of leads generated. • Cost per lead and overall campaign efficiency. • Campaign conversion rates and relevant business outcomes. • Effectiveness of audience targeting and A/B testing. • Advertising budget utilization and optimization. • Accuracy of tracking, reporting, and campaign analysis. • Improvement in lead quality and conversion performance over time. Performance targets will be defined based on the client’s industry, campaign objectives, advertising budget, and historical performance. 6. Ideal Candidate Profile The ideal candidate is a hands-on performance marketer who understands both the technical and strategic aspects of digital advertising. The candidate must be comfortable taking ownership of campaigns from start to finish and making decisions based on data rather than assumptions. 7. Application Requirements Candidates should submit an updated resume highlighting their experience with Meta Ads, Google Ads, and LinkedIn Ads. Shortlisted candidates may be asked to discuss previous campaigns, campaign budgets, targeting strategies, lead quality, and measurable results.

Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience. We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture . We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR. Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond. The M&A and International Expansion role Alan is diversifying its activities in the fields of healthcare, prevention and insurance through mergers and acquisitions, and is actively expanding internationally. In addition, Alan recruits talent worldwide and enables its employees to work remotely in complete safety. “Alaner, everywhere”. The role makes sure each acquisition and each country opening is legally secure, fast and humane: from HR due diligence, to transferring employment contracts, to fully integrating the people who join us. You'll join the Expansion crew inside the People team. You'll work closely with the crew owner, and with Corporate, Finance, team Leads and General Managers involved in each deal. The People team The People team is made up of 13 people who work in an environment shaped by Alan's Leadership Principles. Every one of them is a genuine fan of our products (Culture being one of them) and deeply committed to Alan's Prevention and Health mission. The team covers Learning and Development, Payroll and Admin, Employee Experience and Operational Efficiency, Compliance and Employment Law, Comp and Ben, and now M&A and International Expansion. It is a generalist team: everyone shares three core missions, namely People on-call (answering the day to day questions from Alaners, which is now AI-powered), individual situation management, and HRBP responsibilities. This represents roughly 50% of our time. Then each person owns one or more cross-functional topics depending on their flavour. In your case: M&A and expansion. Your missions On Top Of The Core Missions Shared Across The People Team, You Will Work On a Very Diverse Range Of High-impact Topics You will own to the People workstream of M&A transactions from due diligence to integration, alongside the crew and in close collaboration with the Corporate team, Legal, Finance and the business owners of each deal. Depending on the nature of the deal, you will own: HR due diligence: reviewing headcount, employment contracts, collective agreements, compensation & benefits, liabilities and risks of target companies, and flagging red flags clearly to the deal team; Transferring employment contracts in France and abroad, and choosing the right path for each deal and country; Integrating acquired teams: day-1 and first-months plans, harmonising contracts and benefits, communicating with acquired employees, onboarding them into Alan's way of working; You will support the people transition of acquired teams, working with the crew and leads on team set-up, keeping key talents, and supporting every individual situation with care; Working with external advisors (law firms, HR advisory, relocation and EoR providers): writing clear briefs and challenging their advice. Also Opening new countries on the People side : entity vs employer of record, compliant local contracts, benefits and payroll partners You will handle international relocations and cross-border situations for Alaners moving or working between countries (visas, social security, tax, type of contract); Building reusable playbooks (HR due diligence checklist, integration playbook, "country opening – People" checklist) so each new deal is faster than the last Taking on global and cross-border individual situations (mobility, work from anywhere, sensitive cases) Raising the team's expertise : sharing your knowledge of employment law and M&A practices with the crew and the wider People team Leveraging AI and automation to multiply the impact of your work Outcomes within your first months in the team By 2.5 months: You are autonomous on day-to-day People on-call requests; You have mapped our current M&A and country-opening practices and shared a first list of gaps and quick wins; You have contributed to the People workstream of at least one live deal or country opening (due diligence, contract transfer or integration); You have contributed to our reusable playbook (e.g. HR due diligence checklist); You have shadowed and been reverse-shadowed on individual situation management. By 5 months: Depending on the ongoing projects, you own the People workstream of a deal end to end, from due diligence to integration, with the crew as a sounding board; You have run, or co-run, one talent density assessment and the parting ways cases that came with it; You handle cross-border individual situations without supervision; Your playbooks are used by the crew and by Legal / Finance on new deals; Leads and crew members come to you as the go-to expert on these topics. Is this what you are looking for? You may be a great fit for this role if: You have around 5 years of experience focused on HR M&A and integration topics, for example in a reputable HR advisory firm or in an HR team that focuses on these topics. You have worked on acquisitions in the Tech industry, not only on very large corporate groups, and you know the method is not the same. You master HR due diligence and the transfer of employment contracts. You have worked on post-merger integration, including talent density and parting ways, not only on the pre-signing side. You have international exposure: you have worked on deals or entities outside France. You are fluent in English, written and spoken (all of our internal processes, documentation and communications are in English). You are adaptable and creative: you adjust your method to each type of company and deal instead of copy-pasting one process. You are very organised: you run several confidential workstreams in parallel without dropping balls. You are a strong communicator, with very different audiences (founders, acquired employees, leads, lawyers), in writing and orally. You are strong technically and can teach us things. You show judgement and discretion with confidential information and sensitive human situations. Nice-to-have We are not looking for all of the below. Any one of these can be a strong signal. You have a legal background, ideally in employment law. You have worked in or with a Tech scale-up that made several acquisitions. You have opened entities or set-up employers of record in new countries. You speak another language relevant to our expansion (e.g. Spanish, Portuguese; Arabic). You are AI-enthusiastic and actively use tools to multiply your impact. Level range For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the C0-D level range.
